# Issue workflow safeguards

## No-new-issues freeze - 2026-10-24

Brian's current instruction applies to every local and remote worker: **do not create new issues until Brian explicitly lifts this freeze.** This overrides all earlier bug, audit, qualification, replacement, nested/child, and other ticket-creation instructions in repository guidance, startup prompts, and historical checkpoints, including those preserved below.

Finish existing issues within their agreed scope. Preserve tests, failure evidence, and acceptance criteria; do not weaken tests or close issues with unresolved acceptance. Report newly discovered concerns and blockers to Brian instead of creating replacement or nested issues. Existing ownership, coordination, review, and individual merge-approval requirements still apply.

[AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md#github-issue-organization-and-upkeep) is the canonical policy. Public reporters choose **Report a problem**, **Suggest an idea** or **Something else**. GitHub supplies its normal title field; each form adds one required plain-language description and one optional details box. Reproduction, expected behavior, screenshots and environment can go in that optional box. No form assigns labels or asks for internal planning. The general form is the fallback; the maintenance/validation/improvement choices and internal policy link are removed from the public chooser.

These use GitHub's supported [`textarea` validation](https://docs.github.com/en/communities/using-templates-to-encourage-useful-issues-and-pull-requests/syntax-for-githubs-form-schema#textarea). No `render` option is set, preserving Markdown editing and attachments. A top-level `title` only prefills a default title, so no duplicate title input or synthetic title validation is added. See [issue form syntax](https://docs.github.com/en/communities/using-templates-to-encourage-useful-issues-and-pull-requests/syntax-for-issue-forms). `blank_issues_enabled: false` leaves the three forms available; GitHub still exposes a [maintainer-only blank option](https://docs.github.com/en/communities/using-templates-to-encourage-useful-issues-and-pull-requests/configuring-issue-templates-for-your-repository). API/CLI submissions can bypass forms. These constraints are platform behavior, not additional reporter obligations.

## Intake, origin and readiness

Untriaged public UI/API issues get no internal-checklist feedback, including Brian's hand-written reports. Workers discuss human/unknown-origin requests with Brian first, then enrich agreed scope while preserving the report. [ISSUE_INTAKE.md](../docs/ISSUE_INTAKE.md) defines that gate and worker-controlled creation receipts. Author login/type, prose, labels and body markers do not prove origin; enriching an issue does not change who originally filed it.

Only the exact `triage: complete` label opts into internal checks. Type, area, status, `codex`, `in-progress`, `tracker` and `roadmap` labels alone do not. For public/unknown-origin requests, maintainers add the readiness label after joint review and enrichment, not for initial sorting or worker assignment. Newly agent-created implementation issues must satisfy internal standards and carry the readiness marker from creation within their authorized scope, with a creation receipt. A worker omitting that marker is a policy violation that shared-login author detection cannot reliably fix. Existing internal standards remain; confirm existing decision/readiness evidence before opting older issues into the new checker. No automatic mass relabel is planned.

## Advisory event check

On open, edit, reopen, label, unlabel, transfer or close, the default-branch workflow re-reads the issue via GitHub's API. Per-issue concurrency serializes executions with cancellation disabled; queued events use live state rather than stale payload bodies. Only readiness-marked issues are checked for exactly one recognized type/status, at least one nonempty `area: ` label and the summary categories below. Closed issues and PRs are exempt. The job has only `contents: read` and `issues: write`; checkout does not persist credentials. No repository settings or access changes are required.

The summary check recognizes headings, combined bold bullets, plain labels and equivalent prose. Original criteria retained beneath scoped updates remain valid structural evidence, so legacy issues need no destructive migration. Comments, quoted examples and fenced code are excluded. Empty/placeholder fields are rejected. This is a heuristic presence check: it cannot prove freshness, correctness, revision/denominator completeness, evidence quality, bounded investigation sufficiency or acceptance. Preserved historical text can satisfy structure; human review must reconcile the current summary. Do not treat a clean result as qualification.

An explicit sentence-inline `Completion:` label can also supply criteria after a long scope sentence, including in preserved history. Its first sentence must contain content beyond punctuation, common placeholders or a bare non-acceptance disclaimer; later unrelated discussion cannot fill an empty first sentence. This bounded rule does not attempt general natural-language interpretation. Existing headings, prose cues and comment lifecycle remain unchanged.

Only missing internal requirements create a comment, explicitly addressed to maintainers and agents. New public reports remain silent. If an issue already has an older bot checklist comment but lacks the readiness label, its next normal event updates that comment once to say the reporter needs no additional fields; this does not claim internal compliance. Removing readiness returns validation to intake, not approval or completed work. Subsequent events update the same marked `github-actions[bot]` comment when findings change; identical findings are silent. Correction resolves internal findings, closure marks feedback inactive, and reopening reuses it. Human comments bearing the marker are ignored. No bodies, labels, assignments, claims, issue states or user comments are changed. Feedback contains only fixed text and never quotes issue-controlled content. The trusted default-branch module treats issue text as data; no issue text is interpolated into a shell, script, checkout ref or expression.

API errors fail the action visibly rather than silently claiming compliance. Deleted/locked/transferred issues can cause a failed API request; retry after resolving access/availability. Bot comments remain a best-effort advisory, not a required issue gate. GitHub may coalesce pending events; every execution checks current state, so intermediate transitions need not each get a comment. A manual duplicate workflow outside this concurrency group is unsupported.

## Rollout and review

Publishing a draft PR does not activate these forms or event behavior; an individually approved default-branch merge is still required. Create/verify the exact `triage: complete` repository label before rollout; no public form applies it. Existing issues are evaluated on their next supported event, with no bulk body rewrite, origin inference, relabel or comment backfill. Existing internal issues remain subject to maintainer policy even before readiness opt-in. Human/PAT/API events use the same scoped validator. GitHub suppresses most follow-up events caused by `GITHUB_TOKEN`; automation using it must call the validator directly or leave maintainer follow-up. No new credential or repository-wide token scope is introduced. This change neither configures a duplicate review schedule nor authorizes implementation, merge or deployment.

Events alone cannot refresh parent summaries after merges. The [PR template](pull_request_template.md) and AGENTS.md require the merger to identify affected parents, re-read current issues/comments, prepend/update current summaries with merged revisions and evidence limits, preserve dated history, reconcile remaining/deferred scope, and read back metadata. Close only completed scope or a visible acceptance-bearing transfer. A partial merge leaves a parent open; merge, deployment and independent user acceptance remain separate.

The check's issue-write permission is used solely for its own advisory comment. It grants no agent authority to merge, deploy, operate scanners or claim acceptance. Roll back by reverting the workflow/forms/module in an approved PR; existing feedback comments are retained as history. To check locally without GitHub writes:

```sh
node --test .github/scripts/issue-guidelines.test.cjs
```

After installing development dependencies, Core verification runs this command on every PR. Tests parse the real YAML forms/workflow with the already locked `js-yaml` parser, now an explicit development dependency. They cover minimal rendered reports, sorting versus readiness, shared identities and spoofed origin prose, internal label/legacy-summary checks, untrusted text, live-state readback and repeated/create/update/resolve/close/reopen/return-to-intake behavior. Local schema tests do not claim GitHub server validation, a live form preview, provenance verification or an executed event workflow. Those require separate rollout/operational evidence.
